findings.issue: Sprite resolution (front_default vs id-based fallback) exists in two independent copies; fixing a Deoxys-style sprite bug in one leaves the home grid wrong.
findings.suggestion: Extend buildPokemonCards to also fetch per-card types and use it from the home page, so card assembly lives in exactly one place.

findings.issue: Home page hand-rolls the same card-assembly + type-mapping pipeline that lib/cards.js already provides, drifting the two apart.
findings.suggestion: Reuse buildPokemonCards (with a types option) for the paginated slice; keep only filtering/pagination in the page.

findings.issue: TypeBadge is exported from PokemonCard.jsx but is a general-purpose component used by MovesSection and the moves/types pages, creating an odd dependency direction.
findings.suggestion: Move TypeBadge into its own module (components/TypeBadge.jsx).

findings.issue: Inline regex duplicates idFromUrl from lib/format.js, with subtly different behaviour (returns string vs number).
findings.suggestion: Import idFromUrl and rely on the shared implementation.

findings.issue: The slot-sorted type-to-English mapping block is duplicated in app/app/pokemon/[name]/page.jsx:136-143.
findings.suggestion: Extract a typesOfPokemon(pokemon, typeData) helper into lib/cards.js or lib/format.js.

findings.issue: mediaUrl is exported but never called anywhere — dead code that suggests an abandoned sprite-rewriting layer.
findings.suggestion: Delete it, or use it as the single choke point when sprite paths need rewrites (which would also help the Deoxys-style bug).

findings.issue: EvolutionList is a trivial pass-through wrapper around EvolutionNode, adding indirection with no variation.
findings.suggestion: Collapse to a single recursive component.

findings.issue: export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic' is repeated in every route; a future move to Next 16 Cache Components removes this API entirely, touching all seven files.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable today, but consider centralizing rendering dynamism via a root-level default and tracking the Cache Components migration path.

summary: A conventionally structured App Router app with a genuinely useful card abstraction and clean server/client seams; most edits land in one obvious route file. The main editability tax is duplication between lib/cards.js and the home page's inline card pipeline, which splits one conceptual change (sprites, sorting, types) across two or three files. Fixing that and relocating TypeBadge would lift the codebase from solid to exemplary.

scenarios.change: Remove the Abilities pages and every link to them
scenarios.notes: Delete the route directory, delete the Abilities Section on the Pokémon page, optionally drop getAbility. No nav links or other pages reference abilities, so nothing else surfaces.

scenarios.change: Fix the wrong-sprite bug for species like Deoxys
scenarios.notes: One fix in buildPokemonCards covers the moves/abilities/types lists, but the home grid re-implements sprite resolution at page.jsx:82-85, and the Pokémon page's artwork fallback is a third variant — a single edit does not cover every list of cards.

scenarios.change: Add sorting by name to every list of Pokémon cards
scenarios.notes: Both card builders sort at data-build time (cards.js:27 by id; home filters the species list), and every page renders the array as-is, so two sort tweaks propagate everywhere. The home page must sort before the pagination slice, which is the only subtle spot.

scenarios.change: Add an Items section (/items, /items/:name) shaped like Moves
scenarios.notes: Section, NotFound, TypeBadge, buildPokemonCards and the format helpers all lift over intact, and api.js shows the exact accessor pattern. But the detail-page skeleton (h1, dl panel, Effect section, cards section, generateMetadata 404 handling) is copied, not shared, so roughly half the new code is boilerplate duplication of moves/[name]/page.jsx.

scenarios.change: Change the API base URL and caching rules
scenarios.notes: Base URL, fetch cache option, in-memory promise cache and all per-kind memos live in the single requestJson/apiBase choke point — excellent. The only scattered knowledge is export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic' repeated in all seven routes, which a render-caching change or the Cache Components migration would touch everywhere.
